$schema_note: Product/resource catalog for DigitalOcean. `automatable` here is a resource-level summary; see actions.json for the per-action breakdown and automation.json for the full capability grid.

compute.name: GPU Droplets
compute.notes: No separate resource type — created via the same /v2/droplets endpoint with a GPU-enabled size slug.

compute.name: Bare Metal GPUs
compute.notes: Real, distinct product (dedicated 8-GPU single-tenant servers, NVIDIA HGX H100/H200, AMD MI300X; NYC1/AMS3 only). Zero REST API surface found — sales/contract-provisioned only.

data.name: Managed Databases
data.notes: All 6 engines confirmed real and distinct, one shared API surface distinguished by an `engine` field. Redis is being phased toward Valkey per DigitalOcean's own messaging — do not assume Redis remains a first-class engine long-term.

data.name: Spaces (S3-compatible object storage)
data.notes: Data-plane (buckets/objects) uses a separate S3-compatible host + AWS-Sig-v4 credential. Key management (creation/rotation of that credential) is a SEPARATE, standard-v2-API resource — see auth_methods.spaces_key in provider.json. Corrected 2026-08-17.

networking.name: Load Balancers
networking.notes: "Global Load Balancers" existence as a separate resource vs. a flag on the regional object is unconfirmed.

networking.name: Reserved IPs
networking.notes: Formerly "Floating IPs" (renamed 2022-06-16). Legacy /v2/floating_ips endpoints still function as aliases.

ai.name: Serverless Inference
ai.notes: Stateless call surface (chat/embeddings/images/etc.) — no CRUD/DELETE, nothing to manage as a resource.

ai.name: Batch Inference
ai.notes: Async jobs, 24hr guaranteed completion window, JSONL input <=200MB/50000 requests.
